back: Europe to Africa with goods; Africa to the Americas with captives; the Americas to Europe with plantation produce.
The second leg: the voyage of enslaved Africans across the Atlantic to the Americas.

front: What goods went from Europe to Africa?
back: Cloth, guns and gunpowder, iron and copper goods, alcohol and beads.

front: What goods went from the Americas to Europe?
back: Sugar, tobacco, cotton, rum and coffee.

front: About how many Africans were embarked for the Americas?
back: Historians estimate about 12 million; well over a million died at sea.

front: Which African region supplied the most captives?
back: West-Central Africa (the Kongo and Angola region).

front: Which country received the most enslaved Africans?
Name four features of the Middle Passage.
back: Crowding below decks in chains; disease; violence and abuse; many deaths; and resistance by captives.

front: How did enslaved people resist on plantations?
back: Working slowly, running away (maroons), keeping their culture alive and revolting, as in Saint-Domingue (Haiti, 1791-1804).
